name: Tomato Fruitworm (Corn Earworm)
description: A polyphagous caterpillar pest that feeds on fruits of tomato, pepper, and other crops. The larvae bore into fruits, causing direct damage, fruit rot, and making produce unmarketable.
symptoms: Small entry holes on fruit surface
Larvae feeding inside fruits causing tunnels
Fruit rot and premature fruit drop
Secondary fungal infection developing at feeding sites
treatments: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) when larvae are young
Spray spinosad or emamectin benzoate at fruit set
Use neem-based insecticides every 5-7 days during fruiting
prevention: Monitor with pheromone traps to time insecticide applications
Plant early to avoid peak pest pressure
Intercrop with basil or marigold as repellent plants
Conserve natural enemies (trichogramma wasps, predatory bugs)
Remove volunteer crop plants between seasons
references: NAERLS Tomato and Pepper Pest Management
